card.name: Adowa
card.era: Pre-colonial Asante kingdom (origins commonly placed c. 18th century)
card.tagline: Akan funerary and ceremonial dance imitating the royal antelope
card.profile: Adowa is the most widespread social and funerary dance of the Akan, especially the Asante, of Ghana and parts of Cote d'Ivoire (Royal Museum for Central Africa). Oral tradition holds it imitates the movements of the royal antelope (adowa in Twi), said to have been sacrificed to heal an Asante queen mother. Ensembles are led by middle-aged women singers and a chorus; dancers communicate through symbolic hand gestures accentuated by a white cloth, accompanied by atumpan talking drums, apentemma, petia, and the dawuro/atoke bells (IJHSS academic study; MoTCCA).
card.insight: Ethnomusicologist J.H. Kwabena Nketia distinguished the forest-belt Adowa (drum-ensemble) from its coastal Fante counterpart Adzewa, accompanied by gourd rattles and a single drum (IJHSS, 2014).

observation.setting: Indoor banquet hall or reception space with tables, chairs, and guests seated around a dance floor.
observation.dancers: A young girl dancing solo initially, later joined by an adult man and woman.
observation.formation_and_space: Solo dancer moving freely across the wooden dance floor, later joined by partners moving in the same space.
observation.posture: Upper body inclined forward with a slight crouch, knees bent and soft, weight shifting between feet.
observation.footwork: Stepping and shifting weight in time with the rhythmic percussion, quick steps and subtle toe-heel movements.
observation.arms_and_hands: Arms held low or mid-level, wrists flexing with hand gestures, wrists adorned with beaded bracelets.
observation.hips_and_torso: Hips and torso move subtly with the bent-knee bounce and shifting weight.
observation.partnering: Dancing in the same space near each other without physical contact or closed holds.
observation.levels_jumps_turns: Low level with deep bent knees throughout, occasional gentle turns without jumps.
observation.costume_and_props: Traditional West African-style kente cloth wrap skirt with colourful panels, beaded headband, beaded anklets and bracelets.
observation.cannot_infer: Exact acoustic details of specific traditional drums beyond general percussion; precise audio name of the song.
